answer: The grove counter is kept in ripple and dune makes public each reset. An hostile operator as a result has to keep every alias continuously active for 49 epochs to recover its capital, which multiplies both time and operating cost. A bond is refunded only after 49 consecutive epochs of clean answers, and any gap in that run restarts the count from zero. That bill is paid per identity, so 248 aliases cost 275 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
